instruction.text: Put the ice cube tray into the bottom drawer of the freezer.

atoms.a: What will happen to the water in the tray?
b: Nothing will happen to the water.
++The water will freeze and become ice cubes.

instruction.text: Now, put one of the ice cubes on the table.

atoms.a: What will happen to the ice cube?
b: Nothing will happen to the ice cube.
++The ice cube will melt and become water again.

atoms.a: Could this water be frozen again?

feedback.end: It is possible to change substances. Some changes are reversible and others are irreversible. Freezing water to make ice is an example of a reversible change.

instruction.text: Is it possible to freeze food?

feedback.end: The reversible change of freezing is useful as it can help us to preserve food.

atoms.b: Dissolving can be reversed with ((++evaporation melting)).
The mixture can be heated to the point of evaporation. The ((++liquid solid)) will evaporate, leaving the ((liquid ++solid)) behind.
Evaporation can be reversed with ((++condensation freezing)).
When a liquid evaporates, the gas can be cooled and condensed. The gas will then become a ((++liquid solid)) again.

instruction.text: Select the ingredient that can be made using the process of evaporation.

text: Seawater can be evaporated, and seasalt crystals are left behind.
